The Knowledge Project Podcast

Bing Gordon is the former Chief Creative Officer of Electronic Arts and a partner at Kleiner Perkins.

He served on Amazon’s board for more than a decade, a seat he earned after giving Jeff Bezos five ideas. The first was Amazon Prime. Bing describes the week two directors told him they wanted to resign, and the fix he proposed: Bezos opens each meeting with what’s on his mind, and six-page memos replace slide decks.

He explains Bezos’s first rule for the board, “first, do no harm,” and the “institutional no” Bezos wanted the board to help Amazon avoid. He lays out the three behaviors Bezos looks for in people who are right a lot, why Bezos dropped one-on-ones, and how every Amazon candidate faces a seven-person interview loop built on the leadership principles.

Bing then turns to what games taught him. He explains why moving a game from an 80 to a 90 doubles sales, why Steven Spielberg recut films until nobody left their seat, and how expansion packs for The Sims shaped his pitch for Prime.

He shares the David Ogilvy lessons that never made the books, including that 90% of people who recall an ad remember the headline and only 25% remember the body copy.
